personal_info.summary: I am a passionate software engineer focused on building intelligent web applications, AI integrations, and scalable architectures. I love solving complex problems and turning ideas into impactful digital experiences.

work_experience.about: Seat of Joy is an Indian startup incubated at IIT Madras that developed a safety seat for children specifically designed for two-wheelers — in India, 2 children die every day due to two-wheeler accidents and no existing product provided full-body protection during an accident. Seat of Joy fills that gap.
achievements: Developed a probabilistic market-sizing mathematical model from scratch using Indian Census 2011 data (100+ tables, 200K+ rows each), combining birth-order probability analysis and age-gap distributions with linear regression to estimate 55M target customers with 5% YoY growth — a 45% improvement over the previous estimate, used in all investor pitch decks. The model works by using two census tables: one mapping mother's age to child age-gap from a previous child (second/third births), and another recording whether each birth is a first, second, or higher-order child. Multiplying these probabilities gives the likelihood a given child falls in the 3–6 year target age range, then linear regression projects future growth. When the next census is released the model's 2011-based predictions can be validated against actual data.

Built a supply-chain optimization model using operations research principles (solved via Gurobi and Excel Solver) that maximises profit by balancing manufacturing costs, shipping costs, and selling price — with penalty terms for over-concentrating shipments into one state (elastic-net style) and state-level demand caps derived from the market-sizing model's per-state estimates.

Conducted full competitor analysis — SWOT across three product categories (child safety seats, two-wheeler accessories, and general child restraints) plus direct pricing analysis sourced by calling manufacturers to obtain their production costs — establishing the margin structure of the category and informing Seat of Joy's positioning and launch pricing strategy.

Led a team of 3 to develop the complete business and marketing pitch deck for Shark Tank India Auditions; the deck covered market-size analysis (backed by the mathematical model), competitive landscape, pricing strategy, and go-to-market plan — represented the startup at the auditions and answered all investor questions on the data-backed analysis.
Performed ongoing strategic marketing work: competitor analytics, pricing strategy, market launch strategies, and market analysis — supporting fundraising and product launch planning.

projects.title: Course RAG Pipeline
projects.short_description: Production-deployed agentic RAG system for UCLA MSBA students to query course materials — lecture slides, transcripts, and PDFs — using natural language.
projects.motivation: The UCLA MSBA program runs 4 simultaneous courses (MSA408, MSA409, MSA410, MSA413), each with its own slides, transcripts, homework deadlines, and deliverables spread across a shared Google Drive. Students constantly lose time hunting for information manually. I built a fully agentic RAG system that classifies every query, self-verifies deadline answers to prevent hallucination, supports human-approved file uploads, and can explain exactly which source chunks drove any answer — all deployed at effectively zero infrastructure cost.
achievements: Built a 13-node LangGraph agent with conditional routing across 5 query types: deadline, summary, upload, general Q&A, and source explanation.

Implemented self-verifying deadline extraction: after the LLM extracts a date, the system re-queries ChromaDB with a rephrased search, cross-references results, and surfaces conflicting dates with a confidence indicator — reducing hallucination risk on the most critical query type.

Designed human-in-the-loop file upload flow using LangGraph interrupt-before mechanism with a SQLite checkpointer: LLM proposes a Google Drive folder path with reasoning, user approves or edits before the file is embedded — preventing mis-categorised files from polluting the vector store.

Built deadline-boosted retrieval: chunks containing deadline keywords are tagged with a contains_deadline metadata flag at ingestion; the retriever merges a deadline-filtered query with a general query, deduplicates, and re-ranks — ensuring deadline chunks surface at top even when semantic similarity is not highest.
Implemented dual-provider LLM fallback: Claude Haiku as primary, GPT-4o-mini as fallback, with provider name surfaced in the UI for transparency.

Added OpenAI Vision fallback for scanned PDFs: when PyMuPDF extracts fewer than 30 characters from a page (image-based), the page is sent to GPT-4o-mini Vision with a verbatim-transcription prompt, 25-second per-page timeout, max 2 concurrent vision calls, and an early bail-out after 5 consecutive failures per file.
Deployed on Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VPS (4 CPU, 24GB RAM) using Docker + Caddy + Let's Encrypt + DuckDNS at ~$1–4/month total (effectively just LLM API usage).

Solved 9 distinct production issues during deployment: Oracle iptables blocking ports 80/443 (fixed via iptables -I to insert before REJECT), DuckDNS domain expiry (fixed via cron ping job), Google OAuth credentials not accessible in Docker container (fixed via docker cp), ChromaDB metadata filter returning zero results (added fallback retry without course filter), LangGraph human-in-the-loop needing state persistence (integrated langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite), and more.
projects.technical_details: LangGraph (13-node graph, interrupt-before for human-in-the-loop), FastAPI + WebSocket, ChromaDB (self-hosted), Claude claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 + GPT-4o-mini (fallback), OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536-dim), Google Drive API (OAuth 2.0), PyMuPDF + OpenAI Vision for scanned PDFs, aiosqlite for session persistence, Docker + Docker Compose, Caddy reverse proxy, Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VPS.
projects.architecture: 13-node LangGraph graph: input_handler → router (5-way conditional) → [deadline: retriever → deadline_extractor → deadline_verifier] / [summary: retriever → summary_redirector] / [upload: upload_handler → location_classifier → human_approval_gate (INTERRUPT) → upload_executor] / [general: retriever → general_responder] / [source_explanation: source_explainer] → response_output → END. Agent state tracks 15 fields. Session history persisted in SQLite.

projects.title: Real-Time Queue Wait Time Predictor
projects.short_description: An end-to-end machine learning pipeline predicting real-time theme park ride wait times using Time Series and Gradient Boosting architectures to outperform historical baselines by over 53%.
projects.motivation: Mapblazer is a theme park routing app that optimizes a guest's itinerary based on their preferences. Historically, the routing algorithm relied on 'current' wait times fetched from park APIs. However, because wait times are highly dynamic, a route optimized for 9:00 AM becomes entirely inaccurate by the time a guest reaches their 1:00 PM attraction, causing cascading delays that ruin the itinerary. To solve this, the routing algorithm required accurate future predictions of wait times to anticipate crowd shifts throughout the day. Building these predictive models introduced major data challenges: our dataset spanned less than a full year, meaning standard tree-based models (like XGBoost) couldn't reliably extrapolate pure chronological datetime inputs. To overcome this, I engineered continuous datetime inputs into cyclical, time-agnostic features (like sine/cosine mappings of the hour and month) allowing XGBoost to map underlying daily crowd flow regardless of the specific date. Furthermore, since irregular US holidays drastically disrupt standard crowd cycles, I deployed Facebook Prophet—a dedicated time-series architecture—to explicitly capture holiday effects and benchmark against the XGBoost models.
achievements: Architected an end-to-end Machine Learning pipeline comparing three distinct architectures (Facebook Prophet, XGBoost Local, and XGBoost Global) across 1.5M+ theme park wait time telemetry records.

Engineered advanced cyclical features encoding continuous temporal data into sine/cosine embeddings, ensuring the models mapped seamless chronological transitions without losing edge-case walk-on data.

Outperformed historical baseline prediction accuracy by an incredible 53.8% using a fine-tuned Prophet time-series model, slashing the overall Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 7.08 minutes to just 3.27 minutes.

Effectively eliminated catastrophic prediction failures ('fat tails') by achieving a 90.38% Error Containment Rate (predictions landing strictly within ±10 minutes of reality), heavily outperforming the baseline's 74%.

Slashed 'Severe Misses' (errors > 10 minutes) by a staggering 62.9% utilizing the Prophet architecture, dropping the severe error rate from 25.9% to just 9.6% across the entire 50,000+ sample holdout dataset.

Developed a live API inference harness that synchronously hits the Queue-Times API, computes live temporal features, and generates predictions across all three architectures simultaneously to benchmark live model drift.

key_metrics.severe_error_reduction: 62.9% decrease in predictions missing by >10 minutes
